title: Defeat fixed-template glyph taps and shrink the exposure window: per-session randomised glyph geometry/colour-LSB jitter, one-word-at-a-time reveal with random hold, dimmed wizard backlight, and the 'never put your backup anywhere digital' screen
threat: A passive display-bus tap with an on-implant glyph template matcher (the Ledger implant stored a-z templates at 0x4D00-0x4E40 and matched the SPI stream), plus camera/EM averaging across a periodic refresh (Kuhn: a cached, pixel-identical glyph 'merely assists the eavesdropper'), plus the no-countermeasure photo/shoulder residual.
proposal: (a) In the compositor (after atlas verification, so the SHA-256 pin is untouched), apply a per-session TRNG-chosen sub-cell x/y offset per secret cell, randomised low-order colour bits (within D-04's weight constraints), and if the atlas budget allows, K glyph variants per letter chosen per cell; this makes a byte-exact template matcher miss and forces the implant to carry an OCR, raising its size/power (which D-03 then sees). (b) Offer a one-word-per-page mode (24 frames, each word with its index) with a random 0-300 ms pre-display hold so no single leaked frame carries more than one word and frame boundaries are not USB/host-alignable; keep scroll-to-end. (c) pq1: program the AW99703 to a low brightness during the wizard (REG_LEDMSB/LSB are already written once at init) to cut backlight-rail and driver emission amplitude. (d) Add Trezor's pre-display warning page.
rationale: The implant that actually existed was a fixed-template matcher; cheap per-session rendering diversity is the one software measure that targets it directly, and it is the countermeasure Kuhn identified as the only effective software one against FPD-link TEMPEST. Fewer words per frame and a dimmer, jittered reveal cut both electrical and optical exposure per frame at near-zero cost, and avoid the decoy-frame approach that failed on glass twice (#258).

vendor_precedent: Trezor One single word per frame (legacy/firmware/reset.c:206-231); Trezor core `reset__never_make_digital_copy` warning (core/translations/en.json:2248); Ledger 1.6 'randomized screen-update parameters' (contrast/supply/oscillator) — later found insufficient on the next panel (new-pin-screen 2023); Kuhn PET 2004 randomised glyph colour bits.
risks: Adaptive OCR implants defeat glyph jitter — it raises cost, not impossibility; say so. Jitter must stay inside the constant-weight constraints of D-04 and inside the CT blit (no value-dependent branch). One-word mode lengthens the backup ceremony (24 confirmations); make it the default only if UX testing on the EVT (no LCD on the bench board) accepts it. Dimming must not fall below legibility — the backlight current is content-independent either way, so the gain is amplitude only.
